# implement.py finish must not report a push failure when the commit landed on origin/dev

## Problem statement

`implement.py finish` treats the exit status of `git push` as the sole verdict on
whether the commit reached `origin/dev`. When the push process is interrupted
(timeout, process-group kill, or a late non-zero exit) *after* the remote has
already accepted and updated the ref, `finish` wrongly reports
`git push to dev failed`, resets the work item from `in_progress` to `open`, and
leaves the operator/agent to reconcile a work item whose work is already on
`dev`. That false failure invites duplicate work and blocks the item from
reaching `in_review` even though nothing is left to do.

The fix is to make the push verdict **remote-observed**: before reporting a
failure, `finish` must check whether its commit is actually reachable from
`origin/dev`, and when it is, follow the normal success path (comment, worktree
cleanup/removal, parent-branch sync, `completed`/`in_review`).

## Users

- **Implementation agent** (`/skill:implement`, `implement.py finish`) — as the
  agent finishing a work item, I want a push that actually landed to be
  reported as success, so I do not retry completed work or hand the operator a
  false failure.
- **Epic driver / parent phase** (`implement.py drive`) — as the driver, I want
  a child whose commit is on `dev` to reach a terminal status, so the parent
  does not stall waiting for a child that is in fact finished.
- **Producer / operator** — as the producer, I want the work item state to
  reflect reality (work on `dev` ⇒ `completed`/`in_review`) and the finish
  report to distinguish "push failed", "push landed but the command was
  interrupted", and "push outcome unknown", so manual recovery is only needed
  when it truly is.
- **Audit / release gate** — as post-push verification, I want `in_review` to
  imply that the recorded commit is on `origin/dev`.

Example user stories:

> As an implementation agent, when the push command is killed at the timeout but
> `origin/dev` already points at my commit, I want `finish` to record the commit
> comment and leave the item `in_review` instead of resetting it to `open`.

> As an operator, when `finish` reports a push failure, I want the report to say
> whether the commit was verified absent from `origin/dev` or whether
> verification itself could not run, so I know exactly what recovery is needed.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Remote-observed verdict.** Before `finish` reports a push failure
   (`PushTimeoutError`, process-group kill, or a non-zero `git push` exit that
   is not a non-fast-forward), it verifies whether the commit being pushed is
   reachable from the remote `dev` tip (`git ls-remote origin refs/heads/dev`
   plus a fetch of that ref and `git merge-base --is-ancestor <full-hash>
   <remote-tip>`). The verification is time-bounded, uses only ref/object
   plumbing (it must not invoke the pre-push hook or the test suite), and
   applies to the non-fast-forward retry push as well as the first push.
   *Verification:* unit tests drive each interrupted-push variant and assert
   the verification probe runs before any failure is reported.
2. **Verified-landed = success, not failure.** When verification confirms the
   commit is on `origin/dev`, `finish` completes normally: it records the
   completion comment naming the commit, performs the existing success-path
   cleanup (process cleanup, worktree removal, parent-branch sync), leaves the
   work item `completed`/`in_review` (terminal read-back still passes), and
   marks the report explicitly (e.g. `steps.push.verified_after_failure: true`
   plus the original error text) with an explanatory work-item comment.
   *Verification:* an end-to-end test against a hermetic bare remote + clone
   where the remote already contains the commit and the push hangs past a short
   timeout asserts `report["success"] is True`, the push step is marked
   verified, the commit comment is posted, and the item is `in_review`.
3. **Genuine failure and unknown outcome are preserved and distinguished.**
   When verification finds the commit absent from `origin/dev`, or when
   verification itself fails (e.g. `ls-remote` network error), `finish` still
   fails conservatively: status resets to `open`, the manual-push/worktree
   recovery comment is posted, and the worktree is **retained** (existing
   WL-0MV533YSW004D1E1 behaviour). The message/report distinguishes
   `push failed (commit not on origin/dev)` from
   `push outcome unknown (remote verification failed: <reason>)`, and never
   claims success without positive verification.
   *Verification:* negative tests (remote without the commit; verification
   probe failing) assert the item is reset to `open`, the worktree survives,
   and the distinct wording/report field appears.
4. **Regression coverage.** New tests are hermetic (self-contained bare remote +
   clone under `tmp_path`; no live checkout or live `refs/heads/dev` mutation)
   and cover: interrupted push that landed, interrupted push that did not land,
   verification probe failure, and a sibling push advancing `origin/dev` after
   ours (ancestry, not equality, must be accepted).
   *Verification:* the named tests exist, fail without the fix (or exercise the
   new helper directly), and pass with it.
5. **Documentation.** `skill/implement/SKILL.md` (push timeout / recovery
   section) and `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` describe the
   remote-observed verdict, the three outcomes, and their recovery paths.
   *Verification:* doc review — both files describe the new behaviour and no
   longer state that a timeout always resets the item to `open`.
6. **Full project test suite passes** with the new changes (enforced at the
   dev-push gate). All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,
   including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries.

## Constraints

- **Positive verification only.** Never report success for a commit that was
  not observed on `origin/dev`; this must not weaken the terminal-status
  read-back guarantee (OSL-0MVME1PI5005WU58).
- **No pre-push hook on verification.** The pre-push hook runs the full suite
  (~minutes); verification must use `ls-remote`/`fetch` only and be bounded
  (recommended: ~60 s, short enough not to compound a stalled finish, long
  enough for a healthy remote). A verification fetch only updates
  remote-tracking refs, which the live-repo guard already excludes.
- **Ancestry, not equality.** Sibling sessions may push after ours; the commit
  is considered landed when it is an *ancestor* of the current `origin/dev`
  tip. Resolve the short hash recorded by `git_get_commit_hash()` to a full
  hash before the ancestry check.
- **No force-push, no history rewrite, no `reset --hard`** of the shared main
  checkout; recovery stays additive.
- **Preserve existing behaviour:** non-fast-forward rebase-and-retry
  (WL-0MUYTCF4L000FX3M), worktree retention on genuine failure
  (WL-0MV533YSW004D1E1), pre-push main-checkout mutation guard, and
  `_sync_parent_branch` safe-skip semantics must all keep working.
- **Coordinate, do not duplicate:** the post-*success* ancestry assertion is
  owned by SA-0MVPZG7A0000N66U (parent SA-0MVNQURZM001TKJY). Extract a single
  shared `_verify_commit_on_remote()` helper usable by both directions rather
  than shipping two divergent probes.
- **Test hermeticity:** tests must never mutate the live checkout's refs and
  must not depend on network access.
- **Report fields are additive.** `steps.push` keeps its existing
  `success`/`hash` keys (a cleanup test indexes the literal
  `report["steps"]["push"]` line); the verified-landed marker is a new
  optional key, never a renamed or repurposed one.
- **No workflow-language change:** the item must not alter the documented
  stage/status transitions, only which outcome (success vs failure) `finish`
  selects when the remote says the commit landed.
- **Source of truth:** the fix lands in this repository's
  `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`; the installed runtime copy at
  `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/` only picks it up after
  `scripts/install_pi.sh`.

## Existing state

- `git_push_to_dev()` (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` L5629) spawns
  `git push origin <branch>:refs/heads/dev` in its own process group, with the
  timeout from `_resolve_test_timeout()` (`.pi/test-config.json`
  `timeoutPerCommand`; currently 2700 s, default 600 s). On `TimeoutExpired` it
  process-group-kills the push and raises `PushTimeoutError` (L4667); on a
  non-zero exit it raises `PushNonFastForwardError` when the stderr matches
  non-fast-forward wording, otherwise logs `git push to dev failed` and returns
  `False`. There is no post-failure remote check.
- `phase_finish()` (L11198) Step 6 (L12011) maps a `False` return to
  `RuntimeError("git push to dev failed.")`, posts a manual-push comment on
  `PushTimeoutError`, and the outer `RuntimeError` handler resets status to
  `open`. Steps 6b–8 (process cleanup, worktree removal, parent-branch sync)
  and the `StatusLifecycle(target_stage="in_review")` exit only run after a
  successful push; `_assert_terminal_status()` (L985) then re-reads the store.
- `_recover_non_fast_forward_push()` (L11050) rebases in the worktree, retries
  `git_push_to_dev()`, and reports the rewritten hash. A retry that lands but
  is reported as failed has the same false-failure problem.
- `_sync_parent_branch()` (L7149) already uses
  `git merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD refs/remotes/origin/<parent>`, showing the
  ancestry idiom in use.
- `_assert_commit_on_origin_dev()` (L8084) already performs the post-*success*
  ancestry assertion in **Step 6a** (L12271), which SA-0MVPZG7A0000N66U shipped
  (now completed). It is the only remote check today and it runs *after* a push
  claimed success, so it cannot distinguish "landed but interrupted" from
  "never landed". The new probe must be **extracted** from this helper (one
  shared `_verify_commit_on_remote()`), not added beside it.
- Existing tests: `tests/test_implement_push_timeout.py` (timeout config,
  process-group kill, recoverable state),
  `tests/test_implement_non_fast_forward_recovery.py` (ordering: push precedes
  worktree removal, recovery end-to-end),
  `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_no_diff_status.py` (terminal read-back).
  None simulate "remote already updated, push command interrupted".
- Observed incident (SA-0MUOO5UEB008RXBP): `finish` reported
  `git push to dev failed`, reset the item to `open` and removed the worktree,
  while `origin/dev == dev == 4b25aac4` already contained the new file.
- A companion ToneForge observation (TF-0MUYFYF7Q007BLCX) noted worktree removal
  on a failed push; that ordering has since been fixed (push before removal),
  so no new worktree-lifecycle change is required here beyond retaining it.

## Desired change

1. Add `_verify_commit_on_remote(cwd, commit_hash, timeout=...) -> bool | None`
   in `implement.py`: resolve the full hash, read `origin`'s
   `refs/heads/dev` tip (`git ls-remote`), fetch that ref when the tip differs
   (bounded), and return `True` when `git merge-base --is-ancestor` says the
   commit is reachable, `False` when positively absent, `None` when the probe
   itself failed (network/auth/timeout).
2. Route every non-success push outcome through that probe. Recommended shape:
   have `git_push_to_dev()` raise a distinct "interrupted but verified landed"
   signal (or return an outcome object) rather than `False`/`PushTimeoutError`,
   so `phase_finish` can mark `steps.push.verified_after_failure`, comment, and
   continue on the success path; `_recover_non_fast_forward_push()` handles the
   same signal on its retry.
3. Keep the conservative failure paths unchanged (`open`, manual-push comment,
   worktree retained) with the unknown-outcome wording when the probe returns
   `None`.
4. Extract the probe so the post-success ancestry assertion
   (SA-0MVPZG7A0000N66U) can reuse it, and note the reuse in both items.
5. Document the three outcomes in `skill/implement/SKILL.md` and
   `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`.

**Success metric:** zero false push-failure reports in which the recorded
commit is reachable from `origin/dev`; every genuine failure still names the
commit/branch and leaves recovery state intact.

**Key Files:**

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `git_push_to_dev()` (L5629),
  `PushTimeoutError` (L4667), `_recover_non_fast_forward_push()` (L11050),
  `phase_finish()` Step 6 (L12011), `_assert_commit_on_origin_dev()` (L8084);
  new `_verify_commit_on_remote()` helper shared by both.
- `tests/test_implement_push_timeout.py` — extend interrupted-push coverage;
  or add `tests/test_implement_push_landed_detection.py` for the new
  remote-verdict tests (hermetic bare remote + clone).
- `tests/test_implement_non_fast_forward_recovery.py` — retry-push path must
  also treat a verified-landed interruption as success.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — "Push timeout" section (L1436).
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — finish / push-to-dev guidance (≈ L329–L371;
  the old L235–L253 push-recovery prose now lives in the reference doc).

## Related work

- **SA-0MUH9R74O002MQDU** (completed) — made the push timeout configurable,
  killed hook children, and left recoverable state. This item fixes the false
  verdict that item's design still allows; it must not regress AC1–AC3 there.
- **SA-0MVNQURZM001TKJY** (completed) — concurrent sessions orphaning commits
  via the shared local-dev fast-forward; shipped the per-repository `finish`
  lock and verified local-dev sync. The lock holds across this item's extra
  probe, which only reads refs.
- **SA-0MVPZG7A0000N66U** (completed) — post-*success* ancestry assertion,
  shipped as `_assert_commit_on_origin_dev()` + Step 6a. Complementary
  direction (false success); the probe is extracted from it so the two
  directions share one implementation.
- **SA-0MW22SEMV00230O5** (open, `plan_complete`) — its AC3 converges a
  `finish` whose commit is *already* an ancestor of `origin/dev` before any
  push is attempted (plus transport classification). This item covers the
  complementary path: a push command that ran and was reported as failed.
  Both need the same remote read, so `_verify_commit_on_remote()` is the
  shared probe; neither item should ship a second one.
- **SA-0MW98UNVB0085LFA** (open, `plan_complete`) — attributes a *prior-run*
  commit on an interrupted-push re-run (no new commit created). Distinct
  concern: attribution, not the push verdict this item fixes.
- **SA-0MVLJXS7R000XIFL** (completed) — bounds repeated failing `finish`
  attempts; a false failure fed that loop, so this fix reduces the loop's
  blast radius.
- **SA-0MUIJAHXS003M7BG** (completed) — live-repo guard attribution of
  concurrent-session churn; the verification fetch touches only
  remote-tracking refs, which the guard excludes.
- **SA-0MUY9PSRS003V5CM** (completed) — driven-child worktree escape
  incident; the ToneForge duplicate report (TF-0MUYFYF7Q007BLCX) was split
  from it and supplied the worktree-retention observation.
- **WL-0MV533YSW004D1E1** and **WL-0MUYTCF4L000FX3M** — referenced in the code
  and docs for push-before-removal ordering and non-fast-forward recovery
  (records live in another project's worklog, not resolvable here).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** a push can land yet be reported as failed (observed:
  SA-0MUOO5UEB008RXBP). The verification probe is the correct discriminator;
  it also degrades safely when no such race occurs.
- **Assumption:** `origin` is the canonical remote for `dev`, as assumed
  throughout `implement.py`; no multi-remote support is added.
- **Assumption:** verification is read-only w.r.t. shared refs — a fetch updates
  `refs/remotes/origin/*` only — so it does not trip the main-checkout mutation
  guard.
- **Risk:** the probe's own network call can stall or fail; it is bounded and
  its failure maps to the conservative "unknown" outcome.
- **Risk:** sibling pushes can advance `origin/dev` between probe steps; using
  the freshly read tip and ancestry (not equality) avoids false negatives.
- **Risk:** short-hash ambiguity in the report/comment; resolve to a full hash
  for the check while keeping the short hash in human-facing text.
- **Risk (scope creep):** redesigning the push/lock architecture belongs to
  SA-0MVNQURZM001TKJY; this item only adds the verdict check. Any further
  hardening discovered during implementation is filed as a linked item rather
  than folded in.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required: the seed report, the companion comment,
and repository research supplied enough detail to draft testable acceptance
criteria. The assumptions are recorded above and are open to producer
correction without changing the intent.

- Q: *What is the dominant failure mode being fixed?* — Answer (seed report,
  SA-0MUOO5UEB008RXBP): a push that landed on `origin/dev` while `finish`
  reported `git push to dev failed` and reset the item to `open`. Source:
  work-item description.
- Q: *Does the companion observation (worktree removed on a failed push) still
  need work?* — Answer (repo research): no — Step 6 now runs the push before
  Step 7's worktree removal, so a failed push retains the worktree
  (`implement.py` Step 6–7, L12011–L12360, commit `6229a0605`,
  WL-0MV533YSW004D1E1). Source:
  `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`,
  `tests/test_implement_non_fast_forward_recovery.py::TestFinishOrdering`.
- Q: *Is there an existing post-push remote check to reuse?* — Answer (repo
  research): partially. `_sync_parent_branch()` (L7149) uses
  `git merge-base --is-ancestor` for the local parent branch, and the
  post-success ancestry assertion SA-0MVPZG7A0000N66U **has since landed**
  (completed) as `_assert_commit_on_origin_dev()` (L8084) + Step 6a
  (L12271). Revision: the probe is therefore **extracted** from that helper
  and reused, rather than written fresh beside it.
  Source: `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` L7149, L8084, L12271; work
  item SA-0MVPZG7A0000N66U (completed).
- Q: *Is this a duplicate of an existing item?* — Answer (duplicate check):
  no. SA-0MUH9R74O002MQDU (completed) fixed timeout configuration, process-group
  kill and recoverable state but still treats an interrupted push as a failure;
  SA-0MVPZG7A0000N66U covers the opposite (false-success) direction and is
  completed. Source: `wl show` on both items.

## Plan: changelog

Plan session 2026-11-11 (`/skill:plan SA-0MUOOXH17004ZEFX`). Pre-check:
effort Small / risk Medium → full planning required; approval gate not
requested (approval needs Extra Large **and** High/Severe).

- Decomposed into three dependency-ordered slices, test-first:
  - **SA-0MWCE5XKV0027468** — Hermetic interrupted-push verdict tests (`task`).
  - **SA-0MWCE5ZBR009WC53** — Remote-observed push verdict in finish (`bug`);
    depends on SA-0MWCE5XKV0027468.
  - **SA-0MWCE61RC000L15T** — Document remote-observed push verdict (`docs`);
    depends on SA-0MWCE5ZBR009WC53.
- AC coverage review: 6/6 parent ACs covered (100%); recommendation `proceed`.
- No clarifying questions were needed; the description already carried the
  desired change and constraints, so no producer input was requested.
- Duplicate check: no full duplicate. Partial overlaps recorded in **Related
  work** and kept out of scope — SA-0MW22SEMV00230O5 AC3 (already-landed
  convergence before a push is attempted) and SA-0MW98UNVB0085LFA (prior-run
  commit attribution). Both share `_verify_commit_on_remote()`.
- Conservative corrections applied during the automated review stages: stale
  line references in **Existing state** / **Key Files** (verified against
  HEAD), the corrected status of related items (SA-0MVPZG7A0000N66U,
  SA-0MVNQURZM001TKJY, SA-0MVLJXS7R000XIFL and SA-0MUIJAHXS003M7BG are
  completed), the new `_assert_commit_on_origin_dev()` existing-state bullet,
  and current documentation anchors. No requirement or AC text was changed
  (AC1–AC6 are unchanged).

### Plan-session appendix (questions & answers)

No operator interview was required: the seed description supplied testable acceptance
criteria, a desired change and key files, and repository research answered the remaining
planning questions. Recorded for auditability:

- Q: *Do the child slices already exist?* — Answer (repo research + `wl list --parent`):
  no children existed; three were created (`SA-0MWCE5XKV0027468`,
  `SA-0MWCE5ZBR009WC53`, `SA-0MWCE61RC000L15T`).
- Q: *Which test harness should the new tests use?* — Answer (repo research):
  `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` (`init_bare_remote`, `init_repo`, `add_worktree`,
  `commit_all`), as used by `skill/implement/tests/test_implement_push_from_worktree.py`;
  end-to-end `phase_finish` slices follow the `FakeGitBoundary` style in
  `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_no_diff_status.py`.
- Q: *Is the probe a duplicate of anything already shipped?* — Answer (`wl show` +
  code): partly — `_assert_commit_on_origin_dev()` (L8084) is the post-*success*
  assertion and must be re-pointed at the new shared probe; SA-0MW22SEMV00230O5 AC3
  covers the already-landed-before-push case, so only one probe is added here.
- **OPEN QUESTION: none.** Nothing blocks implementation.

data.description:
# Problem statement

The audit runner's default parent-first flow re-screens gap-mapped children on every parent audit run instead of reusing their content-fresh stored audits, and in `AUDIT_CHILD_IN_MAIN_SLOT` mode (default `true`) it overwrites previously serviced child audits with stale `partial` reports — making parent audits loop forever when children have been serviced but the parent still carries gaps.

## Users

- **Producer/Agent**: Runs parent audits on epics with terminal children; expects serviced child audits to persist and the parent to converge.
- **Herdr/Downtime workers**: Automate audits; they hit infinite loops and destroy good audit verdicts.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Reuse before re-screen.** In the default parent-first flow (`audit_children=False`), when `parent_gaps` is true and a gap-mapped child has a content-fresh stored audit, the parent reuses the child's persisted AC verdicts and does NOT add the child to `pending_children`.
- **AC2 — Serviced audits are never overwritten.** A parent run must never persist a pending-`partial` child report over a child audit that is content-fresh and carries real (non-pending) verdicts.
- **AC3 — Convergence.** After servicing child screens in-main-slot, a parent re-run reports the single unsatisfiable parent AC only (no `Child screens pending` gate) and clears the `<id>.pending-screens.json` signal.
- **AC4 — Regression tests.** Unit tests cover both flows: (a) gap-mapped child reuse skips re-screening, (b) persist does not overwrite a content-fresh serviced child audit. No real `pi` or `audit_runner` subprocess.

## Impact

Agents running parent audits on epics with serviced children no longer hit infinite re-screen loops or lose their hard-won child audit verdicts — parent audits converge on the first clean pass.

## Constraints

- Must not change the `--audit-children` pre-pass behaviour (it already works correctly).
- In-main-slot mode must remain sequential (no parallelism change).
- Changes must be backwards compatible with existing persisted child audits.

## Existing state

`audit_runner.py::_phase_children` (parent-first `else` branch from ~line 14184; gap-mapped child loop at ~line 14240–14330): when `parent_gaps` is true, the `elif child["id"] in gap_child_ids:` branch (~line 14319) unconditionally appends the child to `pending_children` without checking `_get_child_audit_verdict()` or `_child_content_changed()`. The `--audit-children` pre-pass (same function, `audit_children=True`, ~line 13756) already calls `_get_child_audit_verdict()` and reuses fresh audits. In-main-slot mode then emits `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` screens and persists a `partial` child report; a later persist pass overwrites any previously serviced, evidence-backed child audit.

## Desired change

1. **AC1**: In the parent-first gap-mapped path, before adding a child to `pending_children`, consult its stored audit via `_get_child_audit_verdict()` (as the `--audit-children` path does). If content-fresh, adopt the persisted verdicts and skip re-screening.
2. **AC2**: In the persist path for child audits, guard against overwriting a content-fresh child audit. If the target child already has a fresh stored audit with real verdicts, skip persisting the parent-generated pending report.
3. **AC3**: With AC1 + AC2 in place, the `pending-screens.json` signal clears after servicing and the parent converges.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_phase_children` (parent-first gap-mapped child loop ~line 14240–14330; child persist ~line 14438–14475)
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_get_child_audit_verdict()` (~line 8182), `_child_content_changed()` (~line 8864)
- `skill/audit/scripts/persist_audit.py` — `persist_audit()` (the persistence entry point)
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_persist_child_audit()` (~line 7752)
- `skill/audit/tests/` — New/modified tests for gap-mapped reuse and persist-overwrite guards

## Related work

- SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB — the epic whose audit exposed this bug (discovered-from)
- SA-0MVAWFUU0004VW45 / SA-0MVAWFYZE0040SQ3 — unserviced in-main-slot handling (mitigates reporting side only)
- LP-0MVOBJGB4001TQ8X — cross-repo consumer AC that makes the parent permanently partial on this host
- SA-0MSKB6VJA005N43F — opt-in child audit cascade with run cap (context)
- SA-0MW2J7O3D0044SFM — related context (find-related)
- SA-0MU32TE120012T49 — related context (find-related)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions — the root cause, evidence, and acceptance criteria are fully specified in the work item description.

data.description:
## Problem statement

The audit pipeline currently treats *any* failing test as a failure of the audit: a red F3 auto-execution leaves execution-dependent ACs `partial` (so `Ready to close: No`), and a red merge-gate suite run fails the integration closed. That is the right behaviour for the release gate, but it is wrong for the everyday audits an agent runs while implementing a work item: unrelated, pre-existing red unit tests (e.g. another item's broken test) block an otherwise complete item and send the audit into a remediation loop that cannot succeed.

Audits must therefore support two test-failure modes: **strict** (today's behaviour — any failing test fails the audit) and **permissive** (a failing **unit** test that is provably *not affected in any way* by the audited work item's changes does not fail the audit; integration/end-to-end failures always fail).

## Users

- **Agent implementing a work item** — "As an agent running `/skill:audit` on my in-progress item, I want an unrelated red unit test elsewhere in the repo not to block my item, so that I do not chase failures outside my change set."
- **Release engineer (ship skill)** — "As the release gate, I want every audited item to have a genuinely green suite, so that `dev` is never promoted to `main` on the back of excused failures."
- **Producer reviewing an audit** — "As a reviewer, I want the persisted audit report to state which mode was used and, for every excused failure, the evidence that it was unrelated, so that I can trust a permissive pass."

Example user stories:

- Permissive: `tests/test_other_skill.py::test_unrelated` fails; the item only touched `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`; the audit still returns `Ready to close: Yes` with the failure listed as excused (unrelated, unit) and a critical `test-failure` work item created.
- Strict: the same failure blocks the audit; ship re-runs the item under `--strict` and refuses to release.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Mode resolution and default.** `audit_runner.py issue` (and `batch`) accepts `--strict` / `--no-strict`, with `AUDIT_STRICT=1` as the environment equivalent; **the default is permissive**. Precedence is flag > env > default, resolved once and recorded. Unit tests cover the precedence matrix and that `--strict` reproduces today's verdict for a red suite (any failure ⇒ `Ready to close: No`).
2. **Permissive excusal — unrelated unit failures.** In permissive mode, a red suite whose failures are **all** unit-classified **and** proven unrelated to the item's changes does not fail the audit: the runner injects a "run red, excused failures" evidence block into the Phase 1/Phase 2 prompts (so execution-dependent ACs may be marked `met`), the report gains a `## Test Failure Mode` section listing every excused failure with its classification and relatedness evidence, and the `--json` payload carries the same data. Unit tests cover the excused path end-to-end at the verdict level.
3. **Permissive fail-closed cases.** In permissive mode the audit still fails when (a) any failure is integration/end-to-end classified, (b) any unit failure is affected by the item's changes, or (c) relatedness is inconclusive and no baseline comparison can be performed. Unit tests cover each case individually, plus the mixed case (one excusable + one blocking failure ⇒ audit fails).
4. **Scope classification and relatedness algorithm.** Failures are classified by path convention (`tests/integration/**`, `tests/e2e/**`, `tests/manual/**`, `**/*_e2e*`, `**/*integration*` ⇒ integration/end-to-end; everything else ⇒ unit; unclassifiable ⇒ integration, fail closed). Relatedness is decided by deterministic mapping first (failing test file ∈ item's changed files; a module the test imports ∈ changed files; a changed shared test-infrastructure file such as `conftest.py`/`tests/helpers/**`), then — only for inconclusive failures — by a baseline re-run of just those failures in a scratch worktree at the item's pre-change commit (fails identically ⇒ unrelated; passes ⇒ affected). Unit tests cover the pattern table, the import-mapping step, and the baseline comparison (both outcomes), with no real suite execution.
5. **Triage is preserved.** Excused failures are still triaged into critical `test-failure` work items (same dedup + cap semantics as today). Unit tests assert triage is invoked for excused failures as well as blocking ones.
6. **Ship uses strict mode.** All three ship audit call sites (`check-audit-gate.js`, `check-final-validation.js`, `refresh-audits.js`) pass `--strict`, and the manual remediation commands they surface include `--strict`. Tests assert the constructed command strings; the flag name is generic (`--strict`, not `--strict-tests`) so future strictness checks can share it.
7. **Freshness respects mode strength.** A strict run must never reuse a stored permissive "Yes" (it re-runs); a permissive run may reuse a stored strict "Yes". Unit tests cover both directions.
8. **Documentation and validation.** `skill/audit/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`, `skill/ship/SKILL.md` and `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` document both modes, the flag/env precedence, the classification and relatedness rules, and which callers use which mode. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Read-only mandate:** the audit stays read-only except for the existing sanctioned exceptions. The baseline comparison runs only the failing tests, in a scratch worktree (never the main checkout), through the existing paced runner (`run_tests.paced_runner()`) and under the existing `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE` stand-down so nested suite runs cannot recurse.
- **Strict mode must be byte-for-byte today's behaviour** — no verdict change for existing strict callers.
- **Never-block guarantee (F4) is preserved:** the mode never introduces a hard exit for infrastructure failure; inability to classify or baseline degrades to *affected* (fail closed on the verdict), never a crash.
- **The dev-push pre-push full-suite gate is unchanged** — permissive mode does not weaken it; it only governs the audit verdict.
- **Determinism:** the excusal decision must be reproducible from the persisted report alone (mode, classification, mapping/baseline evidence recorded).
- **No new suite executions on the happy path:** a green suite behaves exactly as today; excusal work happens only when the suite is red.
- Scope-creep guard: any richer relatedness heuristic (e.g. coverage-based mapping), or per-repo `unitTestGlobs`/`integrationTestGlobs` configuration, is out of scope — record it as a linked follow-up if it turns out to be needed.

## Existing state

- `_run_tests_via_test_skill()` (F3 auto-execution) parses failures, triages them, and returns `success`; a red run injects **no** GREEN-RUN block, so execution-dependent ACs stay `partial` ⇒ `Ready to close: No`. Red cached entries (`_classify_full_suite_cache` → `red`) also stay partial with no execution.
- `_integrate_into_dev()` (Phase 1 merge gate) runs `run_suite("all")`; `success == False` ⇒ `Integration failed: test suite failed.` ⇒ audit fails closed.
- Green evidence reaches the parent Phase-1 screen, both child Phase-1 screens and every Phase 2 prompt (`_green_run_prompt_block`, `_auto_green_run_prompt_block`, `_test_skill_run_prompt_block`).
- The freshness gate fingerprints `{title_hash, description_hash}` only — it has no notion of *how* a verdict was produced, so a permissive "Yes" would currently satisfy ship's strict re-run.
- Item changed-file resolution already exists (`_resolve_touched_files`, `_extract_key_files`); failure parsing exists (`parse_pytest_failures`, `parse_node_failures`); suite resolution exists (`full_suite_commands`).
- Ship invokes the runner from `check-audit-gate.js:841`, `check-final-validation.js:479`, `refresh-audits.js:131` (`runAuditCommand` defaults), plus the surfaced manual commands in `check-audit-gate.js:386/518/638` and `audit-remediation.js:43`.
- `pytest.ini` declares only `smoke`/`critical`/`benchmark` markers; the repo has no `integration`/`e2e` markers, and `tests/integration/*.mjs` exists — path convention is the practical classifier.

## Desired change

**Headline:** add a `--strict` audit mode (permissive by default) in which only *unrelated unit* failures are excused, and make the ship release gate audit strictly.

1. **Mode plumbing.** New `--strict` / `--no-strict` flags on `issue` and `batch`, `AUDIT_STRICT` env var, default permissive; a resolved `strict: bool` on `_AuditContext`, threaded to the F3 path, the merge gate, the prompt evidence builders, the report assembler and the `--json` payload.
2. **Failure classification + relatedness module** (helpers in `audit_runner.py`):
   - `_classify_test_failure_scope(failure)` → `"unit"` | `"integration"` from the path-pattern table (fail closed to `integration`).
   - `_failure_relatedness(failure, touched_files, key_files, project_root)` → `"affected"` | `"unrelated"` | `"inconclusive"` (test file match, import scan against changed modules, shared test-infrastructure match).
   - `_baseline_unrelated(failures, project_root, baseline_commit)` → per-failure verdicts by re-running only the inconclusive failures in a scratch worktree at the pre-change commit.
3. **Verdict integration.** A single helper (e.g. `_evaluate_red_suite(...)`) that, in strict mode, returns "blocked" for any failure, and in permissive mode returns `blocked` (with reasons) or `excused` (with per-failure evidence). Both the F3 path and the merge gate consume it. Excused-red injects an evidence block analogous to the GREEN-RUN blocks; blocked-red keeps today's behaviour and diagnostics.
4. **Cached-red handling (consistency).** In permissive mode a `red` cached full-suite entry is classified from the cached output (already stored) rather than being accepted as blocking-by-default; if the cached output yields no parseable failure records the runner executes the suite as it does on a miss. Strict mode keeps today's cached-red behaviour unchanged.
5. **Persistence and report.** `## Test Failure Mode` section (mode, resolution source, per-failure classification/relatedness/evidence, baseline commit used); `--json` payload key `test_failure_mode`; the mode is part of the stored audit so the freshness gate can compare mode strength (strict re-runs over permissive; permissive may reuse strict).
6. **Ship wiring.** `--strict` added to the three ship runner invocations and the surfaced manual remediation commands.
7. **Docs.** Audit + ship SKILL files and their `docs/dev/*-reference.md` companions updated with the contract, the default, and the caller matrix.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — mode resolution/plumbing; `_classify_test_failure_scope`, `_failure_relatedness`, `_baseline_unrelated`, `_evaluate_red_suite`; excused-red evidence block; `_run_tests_via_test_skill` and `_integrate_into_dev` integration; report + `--json` sections; freshness mode-strength comparison.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — document both modes, the `--strict`/`AUDIT_STRICT` precedence, default, classification/relatedness rules, caller matrix.
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — full contract: pattern table, relatedness algorithm, baseline worktree rules, cached-red behaviour, mode-strength freshness.
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` — `runAuditCommand` default + surfaced manual commands gain `--strict`.
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-final-validation.js` — `runAuditCommand` default gains `--strict`.
- `skill/ship/scripts/refresh-audits.js` — pre-flight refresh `runAuditCommand` gains `--strict`.
- `skill/ship/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` — state that ship audits strictly.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_strict_mode.py` (new) — mode precedence, classification table, relatedness mapping, baseline comparison, excused/blocked verdicts, triage-on-excusal, cached-red behaviour, freshness mode strength.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_core.py` — extend existing F3/merge-gate coverage for the strict path parity.
- `skill/ship/tests/test_audit_strict_flag.mjs` (new) — command-string assertions for the three ship call sites.
- `command/audit.md` — note that the default is permissive and `--strict` is available (optional, if the prompt enumerates flags).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk: excusal hides a real regression.** Mitigated by fail-closed defaults (integration always fails; affected or inconclusive always fails) and by recording per-failure evidence in the persisted report.
- **Risk: baseline worktree cost/instability** (merge-base unresolvable, worktree add failure, test absent at baseline). Mitigated: baseline runs only the inconclusive failures, and any baseline failure ⇒ treated as affected (fail closed) with the reason recorded.
- **Risk: a permissive "Yes" leaks into the release.** Mitigated by AC6 (ship passes `--strict`) and AC7 (strict never reuses a permissive verdict).
- **Risk: recursion/concurrency** — the baseline run must reuse `paced_runner()` and honour `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE`; tests must mock subprocess execution (per the shared test-writing guidelines: no real suite, no real `audit_runner.py issue` child).
- **Assumption:** "integration/end-to-end" is identified by path convention in this repo (no markers exist); richer classification (markers, per-repo globs) is a follow-up if needed.
- **Assumption:** excused failures still create critical `test-failure` items (triage behaviour unchanged).
- **Assumption:** the merge gate proceeds with integration in permissive mode when the only failures are excused, recording them in the merge-gate evidence (strict keeps failing closed).
- **Assumption:** `--strict` is a generic audit-strictness flag; future strictness checks may join it, so the flag is not named after tests.

## Related work

### Related work items

- **SA-0MSAAUJ1F0026BMN** – Create 'test' skill: run tests, triage failures, validate & fix test usefulness (completed) — the suite execution/triage machinery this change consumes (`run_tests.py`, `parse_pytest_failures`, `check_or_create`).
- **SA-0MUIULX49001BWGG** – Release-gate fail-fast on repository-override vars (completed) — precedent for the release gate taking the conservative path while other callers stay convenient.
- **SA-0MPFD4T0F004RI8I** – CI: Add end-to-end packaging/installation verification for packages/tui (completed) — the end-to-end tests that must never be excused.
- **SA-0MSTN5KRF0097TVP** – F3 default auto-execution on cache miss (referenced throughout `skill/audit/SKILL.md`; the item is not present in this store) — the path whose red result becomes mode-dependent here.
- **SA-0MT456M27001LRTL** – Phase 1 merge gate (referenced throughout `skill/audit/SKILL.md`; the item is not present in this store) — the second red-suite path in scope.
- **SA-0MVIDI8E00063OOP** – Fingerprint from item data only, v2 line (completed) — the freshness gate extended here with mode strength.
- **SA-0MVR9B1UH002BUST** – Audit runner: preserve a producer's review across passing re-audits (open) — touches the same audit-runner verdict/lifecycle surface; check for conflicts when implementing.
- **SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81** – Audit accepts gate-produced full-suite evidence (completed) — the read-only green-evidence path that permissive mode must not weaken.

### Repository file matches

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — the pipeline being extended.
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — audit contract documentation.
- `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` — suite execution, cache scope and triage semantics consumed by the audit.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (mode switch location):** strict default + `--permissive-tests` opt-in / **permissive default + `--strict` in ship** / env-var only. — **Answer (producer, interactive):** option **b** — permissive is the default and ship passes the strict flag; the flag is named **`--strict`** (not `--strict-tests`) so future strictness requirements can share it. Source: interactive reply, this session.
- **Q2 (relatedness test):** deterministic path+import mapping / merge-base baseline re-run / **hybrid**. — **Answer (producer, interactive):** option **c** — deterministic mapping decides the clear cases; only inconclusive failures get the baseline re-run. Source: interactive reply, this session.
- **Q3 (unit vs integration classification):** **path convention** / pytest markers / configurable globs in `.pi/test-config.json`. — **Answer (producer, interactive):** option **a** — path convention. Source: interactive reply, this session. Research: `pytest.ini` declares only `smoke`/`critical`/`benchmark` markers, so marker-based classification has no data to work with today; `tests/integration/*.mjs` exists and is matched by the convention.
